Support functions are continuous, so V is open. At a cutting-sphere point x, (x-c)/a is a unit supporting normal of the ball and of its convex subset L′. At a regular point it must be v, which forces v·x=v·c+a≤h_L(v), contradicting membership in V.

Within the open ball, the two bodies coincide in a neighborhood of each point. A local supporting inequality extends to all of a convex body by considering segments from the point, so local coincidence gives identical supporting normal cones and identical regular marks. The nonregular locus of each full-dimensional convex body is surface-null.

If an exposed-face point x lies in the open ball, then h_L(v)-v·c=v·(x-c)≤|x-c|<a. Since the interior of a convex body is dense in the body, the open ball then intersects int(L), so their intersection contains a nonempty open set. A point only on the closed cutting sphere does not give this strict conclusion.

The strict restriction cannot simply be dropped: for L a ball concentric with and strictly larger than the cutting ball, the physical restriction on the right is zero whereas the cut sphere has positive surface area. No arithmetic constants beyond the radius are needed.

Searched accepted facts on area measures, boundary restriction, exposed faces, ball truncation and normal marking. Existing surface regularity and total area monotonicity do not give this equality on a restricted set of normals.
